sonnet.problem: The opening card says the writer has been 'telling followers of Jesus'. The passage text never says who the readers are, so this fills in who is being spoken to.
sonnet.rule: **Leave open what the text leaves open:** who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The joke puts a modern phone into Moses' scene ('no standing in the back pretending you're busy on your phone that day'). This blends the everyday comparison with the Bible setting instead of keeping the phone as something people do.
sonnet.rule: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

sonnet.problem: Card 7 already showed that Christ did not offer Himself again and again, and card 8 covered the same point. Card 10 asks the same fact again, that Christ appeared once for all and not repeatedly.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.
